title: Is the “Death of Copper” Finally Here? Pat Gelsinger Sees a CPO Boom in 2028 for Two Reasons
gist: A forum post teasing an interview in which Pat Gelsinger predicts co-packaged optics reaches mainstream adoption around 2028, driven by a maturing silicon photonics supply chain and AI infrastructure demand. Only a teaser is given; details are not in the text.

insights.claim: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger believes 2028 could be the turning point for mainstream co-packaged optics adoption, replacing copper interconnects.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Sets a 2028 timeline marker for CPO supply-chain and silicon photonics exposure.

insights.claim: Two forces are pushing CPO toward the mainstream: a maturing silicon photonics supply chain and the explosive demands of AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch silicon photonics ecosystem maturity and AI cluster bandwidth needs as leading indicators.

insights.claim: Gelsinger first predicted the end of copper interconnects twenty years ago, so the timing call has a long history of being early.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Treat the 2028 date with caution given the long-running prediction.

insights.claim: The interview describes a Silicon Valley hardware renaissance, including startups challenging Nvidia's interconnect architecture and companies developing potentially revolutionary AI memory.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Pointer to deep-tech startups in interconnect and memory; specifics are not provided in the post.
